From 543b334d145e59d4379ccdde312bc30c470b1087 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jean Delvare <jdelvare@suse.de>
Date: Mon, 24 Apr 2017 22:07:10 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] virtio_blk: Fix English description of VIRTIO_BLK_SCSI

Signed-off-by: Jean Delvare <jdelvare@suse.de>
Fixes: 97b50a654d5d ("virtio_blk: make SCSI passthrough support configurable")
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@fb.com>

diff --git a/drivers/block/Kconfig b/drivers/block/Kconfig
index f3c2884e05fe..19df4918e37e 100644
--- a/drivers/block/Kconfig
+++ b/drivers/block/Kconfig
@@ -479,7 +479,7 @@ config VIRTIO_BLK_SCSI
 	  Enable support for SCSI passthrough (e.g. the SG_IO ioctl) on
 	  virtio-blk devices.  This is only supported for the legacy
 	  virtio protocol and not enabled by default by any hypervisor.
-	  Your probably want to virtio-scsi instead.
+	  You probably want to use virtio-scsi instead.
 
 config BLK_DEV_RBD
 	tristate "Rados block device (RBD)"
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/block/Kconfig`**
   - The English description for the `VIRTIO_BLK_SCSI` configuration option was modified. 
   - The original line: 
     ```
     Your probably want to virtio-scsi instead.
     ```
     was corrected to:
     ```
     You probably want to use virtio-scsi instead.
     ```

### Relationships
- The modification in the `Kconfig` file addresses a grammatical error in the description of the `VIRTIO_BLK_SCSI` configuration option. This change improves the clarity and correctness of the documentation related to SCSI passthrough support for virtio-blk devices. The patch is part of a broader effort to enhance the codebase, as indicated by the "Fixes" tag referencing a previous commit that introduced the feature.

virtio_blk: Fix English description of VIRTIO_BLK_SCSI

Signed-off-by: Jean Delvare <jdelvare@suse.de>
Fixes: 97b50a654d5d ("virtio_blk: make SCSI passthrough support configurable")
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@fb.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by a grammatical error in the English description of the `VIRTIO_BLK_SCSI` configuration option, which could lead to confusion for users reading the documentation. The incorrect phrase "Your probably want" miscommunicates the intended guidance regarding the use of `virtio-scsi`.

 config BLK_DEV_RBD
